Complete this **10-minute check before Day 1**, using your assigned browser
RStudio account. Nobody needs to install R, CmdStan, Docker or a C++ toolchain.
Teaching assumes basic tidyverse use and previous experience with `lm()`/`glm()`;
tell the instructor if these are unfamiliar. The teaching materials are in English.

1. Open your individual course URL, log in, and open `afec-bayes-2026.Rproj`.
2. Open `day1/exercise-student.qmd` in the editor and run its setup chunk.
3. Run the following code. It reads a supplied result and plots; it does not fit a model.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(posterior)
library(here)
source(here("R/course_utils.R"))
fit <- fit_or_load("day1_seedling", "stan/binomial.stan",
                  list(N = 5, y = 2, a = 1, b = 1), use_precomputed = TRUE)
fit$source
nrow(fit$draws)
mean(fit$draws$p)
quantile(fit$draws$p, c(0.05, 0.95))
plot_update(2, 5)
```

Expected: `precomputed`, 4000 draws, mean near 0.43, an interval near 0.15–0.73,
and a prior/likelihood/posterior plot. Report which step failed and the exact
error message; keep your password private. Save a short note in your workspace,
log out and back in, and check that your note remains.

4. Download and unzip the participant archive **before class**. Open
   `day1/exercise-student.html` and `day1/results.html` locally; check equations,
   figures and tables with the network disconnected. Repeat for Days 2 and 3.
5. Tell the instructor whether login, code, plotting, saved note and local HTML
   all worked. Do this at least several days before 21 October; course times are
   19:00–20:30 China time (UTC+8), 21–23 October 2026.

During class, work in pairs and swap the person running code and the person
interpreting it. Fill `___` before running task chunks. Run only the indicated
chunks. If access fails, use the local handouts and results with your partner.

Optional local R use is allowed after this same stored-result check passes on an
already-prepared machine. Installation is outside classroom time; keep your
Server credentials even if using local R. Live inference requires an
instructor-scheduled slot and is not required for completing the course.
